newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds falter amid thin volume.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds falter amid thin volume.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities recovered a bit from earlier losses but remained under par in late-afternoon trade on Monday.
Mortgage yield spreads widened slightly to Treasuries amid athin-volume session, traders said.
Fixed-coupon pass-through prices were 3/32 to 6/32 lower overall, while comparable Treasuries were off 3/32.
Mortgages took their cue from light selling in Treasury paper earlier in the day.
Traders attributed the Treasury selloff to profit-taking following a U.S. budget deal-related rally on Friday.
Market players also were positioning themselves ahead of Tuesday's and Wednesday's Treasury auctions, traders said.
"It's been very quiet today," said one Ginnie trader in New York. "It's not summer yet but it feels like it," he said, referring to the sluggish activity.
No major bid lists were spotted, and mortgage bankers refrained from selling, according to other traders.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was off 5/32 at 99-15/32, yielding 96 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
